/Issued 421 AM MST Mon Nov 16 2026/ 

 - Meteorological Overview:

For Monday, an upper-level ridge continues to influence most of 
Montana with strong southerly flow aloft. Temperatures will still 
be above normal with dry conditions today until the ridge 
propagates eastward allowing a Pacific shortwave trough to move 
over western CONUS and pivot into Montana by Tuesday night. This 
wave will drive a maritime cold front that will push eastward 
across the Northern Rockies and initiate a surface low pressure 
system over northern Wyoming. The surface low will intensify 
enough to pull colder continentally modified air south into 
Montana lowering snow levels to the surface by Tuesday morning for
north central MT, afternoon for central MT, and Tuesday night 
into Wednesday morning for Southwest MT. This will see a 
transition from rain/snow mix to snow for elevations below 3500 
ft throughout the region however higher elevations will see snow 
earlier. 

For Monday night into Tuesday morning, broad isentropic ascent 
and moderate differential PVA over the region ahead of the 
approaching shortwave trough will, combined with terrain induced 
lift, enhance precipitation over southwest and central MT starting
with higher elevation and mountainous areas. Evaporative and
dynamic cooling will lower snow levels throughout Tuesday bringing
snowfall to the valleys of southwest MT by late Tuesday night.

Tuesday afternoon and evening, 850mb temps from Cut Bank to Great
Falls to Lewistown decrease sharply with the associated cold air 
advection behind the surface low as it moves NE across eastern MT.
Environmental profiles will cool overall as upper level flow 
aloft shifts northwesterly once the shortwave axis propagates over
central MT by early Wednesday morning. As the cold front moves 
through the area, potential mesoscale banding fueled by slantwise 
instability could enhance narrow areas of heavier snowfall along 
the continental divide and northern slopes of the interior 
mountain ranges. 

Wednesday morning, northwesterly flow dominates the region with 
lingering snow bands possible until the early afternoon. This will
bring drier air into the area ending most snowfall and allowing 
dry conditions for Thursday. A weak ridge will build over Montana
for Thursday temporarily until another system moves inland from 
the Pacific on Friday. - RA

 - Forecast Confidence & Scenarios:

From Tuesday morning through Wednesday morning there is high 
confidence in colder modified maritime polar air moving through 
most of Montana. There is medium to high confidence for snow 
levels lowering to the surface for most areas in north central and
central MT by Tuesday evening. There is a 60% chance for total 
snow accumulation of 1 inch or less in the Great Falls area and 2 
inches or less for Cut Bank and Bozeman. Currently, high end 
predictions (90th percentile) have up to 3 inches for Bozeman and
Cut Bank with up to 2 inches for Great Falls, Helena, and West 
Yellowstone. For the mountain passes, total snowfall amounts will 
most likely range from 2 to 4 inches. However, depending on 
strength and duration of a frontogenetical band setting up along 
the divide, there is a 10% chance some passes, including Rogers 
and MacDonald, could see up to 6 to 10 inches. - RA

From Monday night through Wednesday morning there is a 30 to 60% 
chance for 6 inches of snow or greater in the Madison and Gallatin
Mountains, Northwestern Beaverhead County, and along the Southern
Rocky Mountain Front. From Monday night through Wednesday morning
there is a 40 - 80% chance for 4 inches of snow or greater across
the Mountains of North-central, Central, and Southwestern 
Montana. As a result a Winter Weather Advisory was issued for 
Northwest Beaverhead County from 11 PM Monday through 11 PM 
Tuesday. Between Belt and Lewistown along Montana Highway 200/US 
Highway 87 there is a 40 - 60% chance 1 inch of snow or greater 
from Monday night through Wednesday morning. However, that 
probability is too low due to NBM not handling this event very 
well. Most lower-elevation locations of North-central, Central, 
and Southwestern Montana have at least a 50% chance for receiving 
1 inch of snowfall or greater on grassy surfaces Tuesday afternoon
through Wednesday morning. Across Central and Southwestern 
Montana and North-central Montana along and west of I-15 there is 
a 40 - 70% chance for one half inch of total liquid precipitation 
Monday night through Wednesday morning. -IG
